truths.statement: Bats are mammals and the only mammals capable of sustained powered flight
truths.explanation: Their wings are modified forelimbs with a skin membrane

truths.statement: Most bat species use echolocation to navigate and find food

truths.statement: Many bats eat insects and help reduce insect populations
truths.explanation: Insect eating is common among bats though diets vary

truths.statement: Sloths are capable swimmers

truths.statement: Algae can grow in the fur of some sloths

truths.explanation: Adult emperors are larger than other living penguin species

truths.statement: Most shark species are not dangerous to people

truths.statement: Sharks have existed for hundreds of millions of years

misconceptions.statement: All bats are blind

misconceptions.statement: Bats are birds because they fly

misconceptions.statement: Sloths cannot swim

misconceptions.statement: Sharks have skeletons made entirely of bone

misconceptions.statement: Every shark species is a threat to people

misconceptions.statement: Sharks are mammals because they give birth to live young
misconceptions.explanation: Sharks are fish and reproductive methods vary by species

misconceptions.statement: An elephant trunk is only a long nose
misconceptions.explanation: The trunk combines the nose and upper lip and serves many tasks

misconceptions.statement: Asian and African elephants have identical sized ears
misconceptions.explanation: Asian elephants generally have smaller ears

misconceptions.statement: Elephants are born knowing everything their herd knows
misconceptions.explanation: Young elephants learn social and survival behavior within their group

truths.statement: A standard senior football match has two halves of 45 minutes
truths.explanation: The Laws set two equal halves unless competition rules modify their duration

truths.statement: The referee may add time for delays in each half
truths.explanation: Stoppage time accounts for lost playing time

truths.statement: Half time normally lasts no more than 15 minutes
truths.explanation: The Laws set a maximum half time interval

truths.statement: A player cannot be offside directly from a goal kick

truths.statement: Being in an offside position alone is not an offence
truths.explanation: The player must become involved in active play

truths.statement: A player level with the second last opponent is not in an offside position
truths.explanation: The law requires being nearer the goal line than both ball and second last opponent

truths.statement: A ball is out of play only when it has wholly crossed a boundary line or play is stopped by the referee

truths.statement: A ball can remain in play after bouncing off the goalpost

truths.statement: A goal is scored when the whole ball crosses the goal line between the posts and beneath the crossbar

truths.statement: The same Laws of the Game apply worldwide under IFAB

truths.statement: A dropped ball restarts play after certain accidental stoppages

truths.statement: The referee can show a yellow card as a caution

truths.statement: The player taking a penalty kick must kick the ball forward
truths.explanation: The Laws require the ball to be kicked forward

truths.statement: A penalty shootout is separate from the match itself

truths.statement: The goalkeeper must remain on the goal line until the kick is taken

misconceptions.statement: A player is penalized whenever they are standing in an offside position

misconceptions.statement: A player can be offside directly from a goal kick

misconceptions.statement: A player level with the second last opponent is offside
misconceptions.explanation: Being level is not nearer the opponents goal line

misconceptions.statement: The referee must end the match exactly when the displayed clock reaches 90 minutes
misconceptions.explanation: The referee adds time for delays and controls when each half ends

misconceptions.statement: Half time can last as long as teams want
misconceptions.explanation: The Laws normally limit half time to 15 minutes

misconceptions.statement: Every football match has extra time after 90 minutes
misconceptions.explanation: Extra time depends on the competition format and a tied score

misconceptions.statement: A ball touching any part of a boundary line is out
misconceptions.explanation: It is out only when the whole ball crosses the line

misconceptions.statement: A rebound off a goalpost automatically ends play
misconceptions.explanation: The ball remains in play unless it wholly crosses a boundary or play is stopped

misconceptions.statement: A goal counts when most of the ball crosses the goal line
misconceptions.explanation: The whole ball must cross the line

misconceptions.statement: The offside law applies directly from a throw in

misconceptions.statement: A yellow card means the player is sent off

misconceptions.statement: The referee can never add time for substitutions or injuries

misconceptions.statement: The penalty taker may touch the ball twice in a row

misconceptions.statement: The goalkeeper can stand several steps in front of the goal line before a penalty
misconceptions.explanation: The goalkeeper must meet the positioning requirements on the goal line

misconceptions.statement: A penalty shootout is the same thing as a penalty kick during normal play
misconceptions.explanation: Kicks from the penalty mark are a separate procedure used to decide certain tied matches

truths.statement: Our solar system has eight recognised planets

misconceptions.statement: Pluto is one of the eight recognised planets

misconceptions.statement: The Sun orbits Earth once every year

misconceptions.statement: The Sun is the largest star in the universe

misconceptions.statement: Earth has two natural moons

misconceptions.statement: Earth is the only planet in the universe with life

truths.statement: Every flat world map distorts at least one property of Earth

misconceptions.statement: A whale sprays seawater from its mouth when it breathes

misconceptions.statement: Ocean waves carry the same water all the way to shore

misconceptions.statement: A tsunami is simply an unusually high tide

misconceptions.statement: Every ocean wave is created by the Moon

misconceptions.statement: The ocean is salty only because fish release salt

misconceptions.statement: All seawater salt comes from underwater volcanoes
